"We like the balance," Panthers coach Dave Canales said during Monday's teleconference . "There are a lot of variables and it's got to be a part of what we do." It wasn't always that way. During his rookie season, Young predominantly received shotgun snaps and was still sacked a franchise-record 62 times during 16 starts, despite starting deep in the backfield. The extra time didn't rescue the 2023 No. 1 overall NFL Draft pick much during the 2-15 campaign. Enter Canales, hired in '24, in part, to serve as a QB whisperer and designer of a diversified, run-first offense. Now, in their third season together, Young, Canales and first-year playcaller Brad Idzik are creating a scoring juggernaut, despite the running game's sluggish start. item.title: NFL responds to safety concerns surrounding Steelers-Saints game in Paris
item.description: The NFL says the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints are still headed to Paris , even as weeks of student protests raise questions about safety around the historic game. The teams are scheduled to meet Oct. 25 at Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just north of Paris. It will be the first NFL regular-season game played in France. The league said Wednesday that preparations are continuing and that it is working with local officials on security, CBS Sports reported . The game comes during a tense time in France. Students have been protesting poor school conditions, teacher shortages and buildings that need repairs. Demonstrations began in the Paris suburbs before spreading across the country, Associated Press said . Most protesters have remained peaceful, according to the AP, but some demonstrations have turned violent. Police have used tear gas, while some protesters have set fires and thrown objects. Thousands of people have been arrested since the demonstrations began, Newsday said . For now, the unrest has not changed the NFL’s plans. The league said it works with local authorities on security for all of its games, including those played internationally, CBS Pittsburgh reported . With Oct. 25 approaching, the situation in France will remain worth watching. But as of Thursday, the NFL’s message is clear: Paris remains the plan. Read the original article on NJ.com . From the last two seasons combined, the club have spent over £600 million on new talent and, it's still unclear whether they're any better off from it or not. Some deals such as Hugo Ekitike's and Ronald Araujo's have already paid off but, for some, it's still unclear to fans whether those deals were worth agreeing or not. Florian Wirtz is the best example of this because, when he was first signed, he was Liverpool's club-record deal but, just a month or so after, Alexander Isak took that record. This made fans think that their attack was sorted for the next few years but then, this summer, £123 million was spent on Bradley Barcola who's only just finding his feet. item.title: Jaminet stars as Toulon beat Edinburgh in Challenge Cup
item.description: Toulon scored three second-half tries in the Scottish capital [PA Media] Challenge Cup Edinburgh (3) 17 Tries: Ashman, Gwynn Cons: Grayson 2 Pens: Grayson Toulon (6) 27 Tries: Jaminet 2, Tuicuvu Cons: Jaminet 3 Pens: Jaminet 2 Edinburgh suffered their first defeat of the season as they went down to Toulon in their European Challenge Cup opener. Melvyn Jaminet inspired the French side to victory, scoring two tries and contributing 22 points in a superb individual display. The France full-back kicked two penalties, the second from well inside his own half, to give the visitors a 6-0 lead. Edinburgh engineered some good openings but were unable to break through as they were met with some fierce French goal-line defence. James Grayson kicked a penalty to reduce the gap to three points heading into the break. Toulon struck early in the second half when Edinburgh were turned over in the French 22. The ball was spun wide to Jaminet who sprinted free, chipped ahead and gathered to go over for a wonderful score. The home side hit back almost immediately with a cleverly worked set-piece. Ewan Ashman threw to Tom Currie coming through the middle of the lineout. He then set Ashman free to race up the touchline and over the line to make it a three-point game once again. A powerful Toulon maul drove them to the brink of the Edinburgh line before Scotland scrum-half Ben White slipped a lovely little delayed pass to Seta Tuicuvu to crash over. At 20-10 down, the game looked to be slipping away, but Edinburgh responded again when Currie's tackle caused Toulon fly-half Matteo Garcia to fumble in midfield and replacement Geordie Gwynn scooped up and raced free to go in under the posts. Toulon were undeterred, and another rolling maul laid the platform for Jeremy Sinzelle to slip in Jaminet for his second try of the night to all-but end Edinburgh's resistance. Replacements: Jerry Blyth-Lafferty, Jamie Stewart, Paul Hill, Grant Gilchrist, Euan McVie, Conor McAlpine, Geordie Gwynn, Rory McHaffie. Toulon : Melvyn Jaminet, Seta Tuicuvu, Antoine Frisch, Jeremy Sinzelle, Apete Narogo, Mateo Garcia, Ben White; Jean-Baptiste Gros, Gianmarco Lucchesi, Beka Gigashvili, Swan Rebbadj, Corentin Mezou, Zach Mercer, Estaban Abadie, Patrick Tuifua. Replacements: Teddy Baubigny, Samuel Jean-Christophe, Owen Sorhaindo, Luciano Asevedo, Lewis Ludlam, Joe Quere Karaba, Baptiste Serin, Luka Keletaona. Referee : Ben Breakspear

item.title: DeVonta Smith Is Set To Return From Injury, But Is He A Fantasy Football Start With Jalen Hurts OUT
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) makes a catch during pre-game warmups against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Philadelphia Eagles will be getting some much-needed reinforcements in Week 6 after removing wide receiver DeVonta Smith from the injury report. He has not played since Week 3 due to a hamstring injury. After still being a legitimate question mark all week, he is now good to go for Week 6. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is good to go for Week 6. pic.twitter.com/at8wHohsQA - Yahoo Fantasy Sports (@YahooFantasy) October 16, 2026 Smith returns to a team that will be without Jalen Hurts, who was diagnosed with a blood clot this week, and Saquon Barkley, who is sidelined with a hamstring injury of his own. The Eagles' offense could struggle to move the ball with Hurts sidelined. Philly will play the Carolina Panthers in Week 6. Fantasy Impact WR DeVonta Smith, Philadelphia Eagles This is fantastic news for fantasy football owners, even if he's returning to less -than-ideal circumstances. There is definitely concern that his value will be capped by a backup quarterback, but he is still going right back into our starting lineups this week with all the injuries and bye weeks. If he does struggle, it will be a major concern moving forward, because we have no idea when Hurts will be able to return. It's not impossible that his season is over, depending on whether or not he has to be put on blood thinners. However, that could also very well not happen, so we will have to monitor him closely until we get more definitive information. item.description: Portage County's two Chagrin Valley Conference teams meet at Jack Lambert Stadium Friday night. Yes, it's Crestwood and Rootstown meeting for the second time as CVC rivals before both teams make their way to the Greater Portage Athletic Conference in 2027. Check out our preview information with live in-game updates to be added throughout the evening: Watch Ohio High School Football Live on NFHS Network all year Tale of the tape between Rootstown and Crestwood football School Last week 2025 record Last postseason berth Rootstown (3-5, 0-4) L 35-14 vs. Conneaut 6-4 2024 Crestwood (2-6, 1-3) W 28-21 at Fairview 3-7 2023 The Red Devils and Rovers have played every year since 2015, be it in the Portage Trail Conference (2015-2019), as nonleague foes (2020-2024) or as Chagrin Valley Conference counterparts (2025-2026). Their last three games have been highly competitive, all decided by 18 points or fewer. Rootstown won in 2023 (42-30) and 2025 (21-12) while Crestwood prevailed in 2024 (20-2). Meet the Rootstown Rovers football team The Rovers have dropped two straight (and four of five), yielding a combined 92 points to Berkshire and Conneaut. There were encouraging signs from last week's loss to the Spartans. Rootstown amassed a solid 372 yards of offense (200 rushing, 172 passing), with 273 of those yards coming from Blake Mullaly (172 passing, 101 rushing). Max McEwuen continues to be a playmaker for the Rovers with two more touchdowns against the Spartans while Grayson Rantilla added 66 receiving yards. Meet the Crestwood Red Devils football team The Red Devils snapped a three-game skid last week with a 28-21 victory over Fairview. Crestwood was run-heavy with three ball-carriers getting double-digit carries: Christopher Mory (12 carries, 137 yards, TD), Nick Hess (14 carries, 121 yards, TD) and Michael Kalista (19 carries, 46 yards, 2 TD). James Lancaster and Hess added double-digit tackles. Splitting the carries has become par for the course as Hess, Kalista and Mory are all above 650 rushing yards this season. item.title: Troy Aikman’s Dolphins consultant role contractually in limbo
item.description: Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Troy Aikman has made it clear in recent days that his time with ESPN might be ending when his contract expires in March. His Miami Dolphins consultancy role also appears to be up in the air. According to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports, Aikman does not have a “formal and ongoing agreement” with the Dolphins regarding his formal advisory role as a consultant to the NFL club. “It’s not known to what extent, if at all, Aikman continues to advise the Dolphins based on his relationships with owner Stephen Ross, coach Jeff Hafley, and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan,” wrote Maske. “But if that’s occurring, it’s not a formal arrangement, according to the source, who told FOS that Aikman’s official consulting role with the Dolphins was limited to the team’s searches that resulted in the hirings of Sullivan and Hafley this past offseason.” It’s unclear if Aikman was planning on continuing that role following this NFL season, though the league did announce that he would face similar restrictions as those placed on Tom Brady , limiting his direct access to teams, players, and coaches in the week leading up to the Monday Night Football game he would be calling. While he remains eligible to broadcast games involving the Dolphins, the NFL’s tampering and gambling policies very much apply to him. Aikman griped that the restrictions were unnecessary , since they didn’t create a conflict of interest, while admitting the Dolphins hired him for his unique access to information as a broadcaster . As for how any of this affects Aikman’s future, it’s hard to say right now. If he wants to move into a full-time front-office role, he’s unlikely to earn a salary anywhere close to what he makes calling games. If he left ESPN, would the Dolphins want to make his role more permanent, especially considering his strong relationships with owner Stephen Ross and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan? And if he’s trying to set a market for his services as a broadcaster, who knows if any other network or streamer might object to the perceived conflict between the two roles. As with so many things surrounding Troy Aikman right now, we’re all waiting to see how it develops. item.title: OKC Thunder call bluff on Spanish club's legal threats over Aday Mara
item.description: You gotta give Aday Mara's old Spanish club credit — they love some theatrics. Not even a full day after he finished a superb preseason, Basket Zaragoza is threatening to take legal action over the Oklahoma City Thunder and the NBA if he suits up for Opening Night in five days. Now, how much power do they have in enforcing that? Remains to be seen, but not a lot. Mara played with Basket Zaragoza from 2021-23. Five years later, they apparently still have his playing rights. Never mind the fact that he played for UCLA and Michigan in three collegiate seasons since then. The Spanish club has reached out to the Thunder, the NBA and FIBA over Mara's status. And from the reactions afterward, it looks like their threats have fallen on deaf ears. I guess we'll see if OKC's play to call its bluff will work out. As of now, expect the 21-year-old to play from the jump. The Thunder released an official statement — through several NBA reporters — in response to the situation. Here's what they said about the possible legal actions over Mara: "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA." The Thunder added Mara with the No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. He enjoyed a breakout collegiate season at Michigan. Alongside Yaxel Lendeborg and Morez Johnson Jr., the three-headed frontcourt monster helped the Wolverines win a 2026 national championship. Do I think the Thunder will oblige the Spanish club's hilariosuly-timed request? No. Probably not. The NCAA didn't when UCLA went through the same song and dance when Mara first moved to the United States. That said, can't deny that this isn't the type of distraction you need if you're hoping to be a title contender. It hasn't taken long for Mara to tease his NBA potential on the Thunder. He was arguably one of the biggest impact players throughout the preseason. On both ends of the floor, too. To the point that you have to wonder if the 7-foot-3 giant can help OKC as soon as the first day of the 2026-27 regular season. Now, how much power do they have in enforcing that? Remains to be seen, but not a lot. Mara played with Basket Zaragoza from 2021-23. Five years later, they apparently still have his playing rights. Never mind the fact that he played for UCLA and Michigan in three collegiate seasons since then. The Spanish club has reached out to the Thunder, the NBA and FIBA over Mara's status. And from the reactions afterward, it looks like their threats have fallen on deaf ears. I guess we'll see if OKC's play to call its bluff will work out. As of now, expect the 21-year-old to play from the jump. The Thunder released an official statement — through several NBA reporters — in response to the situation. Here's what they said about the possible legal actions over Mara: "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA." The Thunder added Mara with the No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. He enjoyed a breakout collegiate season at Michigan. Alongside Yaxel Lendeborg and Morez Johnson Jr., the three-headed frontcourt monster helped the Wolverines win a 2026 national championship. Do I think the Thunder will oblige the Spanish club's hilariosuly-timed request? No. Probably not. The NCAA didn't when UCLA went through the same song and dance when Mara first moved to the United States. That said, can't deny that this isn't the type of distraction you need if you're hoping to be a title contender. It hasn't taken long for Mara to tease his NBA potential on the Thunder. He was arguably one of the biggest impact players throughout the preseason. On both ends of the floor, too. To the point that you have to wonder if the 7-foot-3 giant can help OKC as soon as the first day of the 2026-27 regular season. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations. Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea are the Premier League’s most fun team but is it sustainable?
item.description: Xabi Alonso’s side are scoring and conceding at a remarkable rate. It’s great for neutrals but not necessarily the best way to qualify for Europe By WhoScored Watching Chelsea this season ought to come with a health warning. Goals arrive in abundance, leads are established before spectators have settled into their seats and clean sheets have become an alien concept. Xabi Alonso has transformed Chelsea into one of the Premier League’s most thrilling spectacles. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 13. That’s 4.7 goals per game in six matches. Chelsea are a neutral’s dream, but is it sustainable? They have scored 15 goals from an expected goals total of just 8.4, an over-performance of 6.6. Their 18.3% conversion rate is second only to Manchester City’s 19.1%, while eight of their 15 goals have come from shots with xG below 0.13. The five goals against Bournemouth last weekend came from an xG of just 0.75. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: FC Copenhagen Women have a ‘startup-like’ brand. Now they need results
item.description: A famous name and record attendances have given FCK a platform but a difficult start in Denmark’s top-flight shows success on the pitch is not guaranteed On an August day in 2024, 5,165 fans gathered at Vanløse Idrætspark to watch FC Copenhagen (FCK) take on B73 Slagelse in their first league match. For Denmark’s most successful men’s club, with 16 league titles, it marked the realisation of their desire to establish a women’s team, through collaboration with the existing FC Damsø, and an ambitious project with aims of having a wide-reaching impact on and off the pitch. The 26 months since have brought a whirlwind of success, the club securing back-to-back promotions to reach the A-Liga. Now they are in the top division and “playing with the big dogs”, as their head of women’s football, Romaney Pinnock, coins it, and they must adapt to stay there. Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
item.description: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. It was an amazing way to go out on a high.” Five months later McKenna has no regrets about electing to cut things short while the going was so good. The golf bag lying outside his garage speaks of a man enjoying the break and, more pertinently, of something bigger. His son has recently become interested in the sport and sharing those moments with loved ones, whether out on the greens or spending part of the summer travelling along the East Anglian coastline in a camper van, were among the biggest reasons to pause a soaring career. At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
